day_shape: 61 items: third tanker reported ablaze east of Hormuz within 24 hours with third US carrier arriving, IDF strikes Hezbollah weapons shipment in Beqaa, Bessent predicts 25% Iran contraction, UK joins Gaza joint statement, heavy Khamenei/IRIB tree-planting cycle.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents and blockade
threads.summary: Iran's army public relations, cited by Defa Press, said a third tanker east of the Strait of Hormuz struck a mine and caught fire within 24 hours, with the IRGC attributing two earlier blasts to mines. Iran International reported a third US aircraft carrier joined the Iran blockade as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent predicted a 25% Iranian economic contraction.

threads.label: IDF strikes Hezbollah in Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF confirmed overnight Israeli Air Force strikes on a Hezbollah weapons shipment in the Janta area of Lebanon's Beqaa Valley near the Syrian border, the first strike in the area in months. The IDF also reported demolishing a 35-metre Hezbollah tunnel in Majdal Zoun and detaining two Lebanese brothers near Shebaa.

threads.label: Gaza operations and Nasser Hospital strike
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet named three Hamas operatives killed in Thursday's Nasser Hospital strike in Khan Younis, including an October 7 participant linked to the abduction of Adina Moshe. The IDF also reported demolishing a 300-metre tunnel on the Israeli side of Gaza's Yellow Line, as UK, Australia, Canada and Italy issued a joint foreign ministers' statement on Gaza.

threads.label: Iraq confronts Iran-backed militias
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi preparing to confront Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah, calling it a potential turning point for Baghdad's authority over militias. IRIB reported Iraq's Media and Communications Commission blocked Telegram on the prime minister's order, giving the platform 30 days to comply with national regulations.

threads.label: Khamenei messaging and regime cultural cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a '13 Aban' quote on the 'heavy cost of miscalculations' by the US and allies, alongside elegy recitations for 'Iran's martyr' and clerical lectures. IRIB and Defa Press ran heavy coverage of a Tehran campaign to plant 313,000 saplings with IRGC cooperation and a book launch of poems by the 'martyred leader'.

threads.label: Iran diplomacy and infrastructure attribution pushback
threads.summary: Defa Press reported FM Abbas Araghchi, in Islamabad for the 30th ECO foreign ministers' meeting, held a phone call with Russia's Sergey Lavrov. Defa Press also published a piece framing the cyberattack on French supermarket refrigeration attributed to Iran as a possible 'false flag' and discrediting project.

threads.label: Iran domestic strains and UK-linked IRGC reporting
threads.summary: Iran International reported five job-seekers arrested after protesting at a southwestern oil company, 12 gas-refinery workers killed in a western Iran bus crash, and a state-linked shipping firm selling a vessel for under $6 million to sons of Ali Shamkhani. The Telegraph, via Iran International, reported Tony Blair's sister-in-law attended an Iran conference US authorities later identified as an IRGC intelligence-recruitment platform.

events.title_en: Iran's struggle with global imperialism from the Mosaddegh government to the Islamic Revolution
events.summary_en: Iran's struggle with global imperialism from the Mosaddegh government to the Islamic Revolution. Economic pressures and naval blockade of Iran by the United States bear similarities to British policy in the early 1930s, following the nationalisation of Iran's oil industry under the leadership of Dr Mohammad Mosaddegh. However, an important difference in current conditions from that period is Iran's ability to confront external pressures through asymmetric warfare and disruption of global energy markets. According to Erik Lob, researcher on Iran's relations with the world, current conditions also resemble that period in some respects. The Donald Trump administration, after failing to achieve its goals through direct military force, has focused on naval blockade and economic isolation...

events.title: The IDF confirms striking a weapons shipment destined for Hezbollah in eastern Lebanon overnight. In a statement, the military says the Israeli Air Force bombed the shipment of weapons in the Janta area in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, close to the Syrian border, after it had been transferred from Syria into Lebanon, en route to Hezbollah. "The weapons were intended to strengthen Hezbollah's operational capabilities to carry out terror attacks against Israeli civilians and IDF troops," the military says. The IDF says that the Janta area has been used by Hezbollah to conduct "numerous weapons shipments" in the past.

events.title: The IDF says it recently demolished a 35-meter-long Hezbollah tunnel in the southern Lebanon town of Majdal Zoun. The tunnel was located during operations of the 300th "Baram" Regional Brigade in the area. The IDF says the tunnel featured two rooms where Hezbollah operatives would reside in. After it was scanned, combat engineers of the elite Yahalom unit blew up the tunnel, the military says, attaching footage of the demolition.
events.summary:
The IDF says it recently demolished a 35-meter-long Hezbollah tunnel in the southern Lebanon town of Majdal Zoun.

The tunnel was located during operations of the 300th "Baram" Regional Brigade in the area.

The IDF says the tunnel featured two rooms where Hezbollah operatives would reside in. 

After it was scanned, combat engineers of the elite Yahalom unit blew up the tunnel, the military says, attaching footage of the demolition.
